parts.text:
The rain slashes against the tempered glass of the skylight, masking the faint hum of my laser cutter. I catch the heavy pane before it drops, setting it down silently on the roof of the Eclipse Corporation headquarters. 

*Echo-12 is in.*

I drop through the breach, landing softly on the steel grating of a maintenance catwalk in Sector 4. Below me, the facility is a hive of sterile white lights and matte-black architecture. I press myself into the shadows as a pair of Eclipse security contractors stride past. They’re wearing heavy tactical gear, assault rifles slung tight to their chests. Rumor is Eclipse recruits them from black-site military prisons; they don't ask questions, and they don't leave survivors. 

I pull up my wrist-comp, bringing up the message from my contact: *The architect's design is flawed, but the blueprint remains. Seek out the anomaly in the Nexus Protocol.*

I’ve spent the last three days analyzing those words. "The architect" likely refers to Dr. Aris Thorne, Eclipse’s former head of R&D who mysteriously vanished six months ago. If his design is flawed, but the *blueprint* remains, it means the current iteration of Project Nexus is built on top of Thorne’s original, hidden framework. I need to find the foundational code. 

I bypass a biometric scanner on a sub-level stairwell by splicing into the junction box and feeding it a looped heartbeat and retinal scan of an executive I skimmed yesterday. The heavy door hisses open. 

I descend into the belly of the beast: the Sub-Level 3 Server Farm. The temperature drops by ten degrees, the air thick with the hum of quantum processors. 

I slip between the towering data racks, keeping an eye out for the automated sentry drones that patrol the aisles. Finding a primary access terminal, I jack in my decryptor drive. The screen flares to life, bathing my face in a pale blue glow. 

Eclipse’s ICE (Intrusion Countermeasures Electronics) is aggressive. It immediately tries to fry my drive, but I deploy a ghost-worm to distract the system, buying me exactly three minutes of unrestricted access.

*Seek out the anomaly in the Nexus Protocol.*

I pull up the massive directory for Project Nexus. It looks like a standard, albeit highly advanced, predictive algorithm designed for global market forecasting. But that's just the surface. Following the cryptic clue, I run a comparative diagnostic between the current live protocol and the archived "blueprint" files from Dr. Thorne's original tenure.

There it is. The anomaly.

Hidden deep within the millions of lines of code is a micro-fracture—a recursive loop that doesn't belong in a forecasting model. It's a backdoor, intentionally left by Thorne. I execute the loop.

The screen flickers, and the facade of the market forecasting algorithm melts away. The true nature of Project Nexus begins to scroll across my screen. 

My blood runs cold.

Nexus isn't predicting markets. It's predicting *people*. It’s a neural-mapping network designed to interface with the micro-tech embedded in civilian identification chips. Eclipse isn't just trying to forecast human behavior; they are building a system to subtly alter it. To control purchasing, voting, and even emotional responses on a mass scale. 

And the "flaw" Thorne mentioned? The system requires a massive amount of biological processing power to stabilize. Eclipse has been using the lower levels of this very facility as a black-site prison, hooking undocumented individuals into the mainframe as living servers.

I hit download, transferring the decrypted files to my secure drive. 

*90%... 95%... 100%.*

Suddenly, the pale blue light of the terminal flashes violent red. 

**"UNAUTHORIZED ACCESS DETECTED. SECTOR 3 LOCKDOWN INITIATED."**

The automated voice echoes through the server farm. The heavy blast doors at the end of the aisle slam shut. I hear the distinct click-clack of combat boots hitting the metal floor grates above. The security team is converging. 

I yank my decryptor from the port. I have the truth. I have the blueprint. Now, Echo-12 just has to survive long enough to show the world. 

I draw my suppressed sidearm, slip a flashbang from my tactical vest, and fade back into the shadows of the server racks. The hunt is on.

The red emergency strobes paint the server farm in jagged, bloody flashes. The heavy thud of Eclipse tactical boots reverberates through the floor grating, growing louder, tightening the net around my position. 

I press my back against the chilling metal of a server rack, my suppressed sidearm raised. My wrist-comp vibrates violently against my forearm. It’s a real-time intercept from Eclipse’s internal security network—the automated threat-assessment scripts triggering in response to my intrusion. 

Two fragmented code blocks scroll across my tiny screen:

**[Intercept: Block A]**
*// Fragmented Script Notes*
*// Eclipse Corporation*
*// Nexus Protocol*
*// Infiltration Vector: Social Engineering*
*// Target: Nexus Project Lead*
*// Anomaly: Unusual Pattern in Protocol*
*// Recommendation: Further Investigation Required*

**[Intercept: Block B]**
*// Fragmented Script Notes*
*// Eclipse Corporation*
*// Nexus Protocol*
*// Infiltration Vector: Data Exfiltration*
*// Target: Nexus Project Database*
*// Anomaly: Unauthorized Access*
*// Recommendation: Immediate Action Required*

I grit my teeth, processing the data while keeping one eye on the aisle. 

**Block B** is me. The system has perfectly categorized my current breach. "Data Exfiltration" at the "Nexus Project Database." The "Immediate Action Required" tag means the guards aren't just sweeping the area; they have a pinpoint location on the terminal I just used. They are converging exactly on my coordinates with zero-tolerance kill orders.

But **Block A**... that's the key. That anomaly log predates my hack. "Infiltration Vector: Social Engineering" targeting the "Nexus Project Lead." This means my contact didn't just stumble upon Thorne's old blueprint; they actively manipulated the current Project Lead to confirm the "Unusual Pattern" still existed in the live code. Eclipse's internal systems flagged the social engineering attempt, but only recommended "Further Investigation." They didn't realize how critical that breach was until I just triggered the backdoor.

I can use this. Eclipse AI is rigid; it prioritizes active, high-level threats. 

I pull a micro-transmitter from my pouch and plug it into a secondary port on the rack behind me. My fingers fly across my wrist-comp, writing a quick, dirty script. If Eclipse's system is already nervous about a "Social Engineering" threat against the Project Lead, I'll give them a reason to panic. 

I compile a ghost-signal mimicking a massive, localized communications blackout in the Executive Suites on Level 1—specifically, the Project Lead's office. I tag the spoofed data packet with the exact signature of the anomaly from Block A. 

I hit *Execute*. 

Instantly, the automated PA system switches tracks. 

**"ALERT. SECTOR 1 EXECUTIVE WING. CRITICAL ANOMALY DETECTED. PROJECT LEAD SECURE-COMMS SEVERED. RE-ROUTING PRIMARY TACTICAL SQUADS TO LEVEL 1. IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED."**

The heavy boots stomping toward my aisle suddenly halt. I hear barked orders over their encrypted comms. 

"Command, this is Strike Team Alpha. We have a ghost in the server room, but system is flagging a direct hit on the Director upstairs. Advise."
"Alpha, leave two men on the servers. The rest of you, get to Level 1 *now*. Secure the package."

The majority of the footsteps pivot and sprint back toward the stairwell. Only two guards left. 

I slide the flashbang from my vest, pull the pin, and toss it around the corner of the server rack. 

*Crack-BANG.*

The blinding white light and deafening concussive wave fill the aisle. I pivot out from cover before the light even fades, my sidearm tracking the two disoriented guards. Two muffled *thwips* from my silencer, and they drop to the grating, their armor absorbing the non-lethal shock-rounds. They'll be out for hours. 

I step over them, moving fast toward the maintenance shaft at the rear of the farm. I have the blueprint. I know what Nexus is. And thanks to their own security logs, I know my contact's cover might be blown. 

Echo-12 is going dark. Time to get this data to the outside world.
Reconstruct the fragmented visual clues to uncover the truth behind the anonymous message. Stay strictly in the persona and world established in the audio recording.

The rungs of the maintenance shaft are slick with condensation, but the adrenaline pumping through my veins makes the climb effortless. I wedge myself into a narrow alcove between Sub-Level 2 and 1, the distant wail of Eclipse security sirens echoing beneath me. I have a few minutes before they realize my ghost-signal on Level 1 was a decoy and sweep these shafts. 

I pull up my wrist-comp. The decrypted Nexus files are safely partitioned, but my mind is racing, snagged on those two intercepted security logs. I overlay the fragmented visual clues—Block A and Block B—with the horrifying truth I just uncovered about the human server farm. 

I need to understand exactly what I’ve stepped into. 

**Block B** is textbook. *Infiltration Vector: Data Exfiltration. Target: Nexus Project Database. Anomaly: Unauthorized Access.* That’s me. That’s Echo-12 cracking the server farm tonight. The system saw me, categorized my physical hack, and demanded *Immediate Action*. 

But **Block A**... that’s the phantom. 

*Infiltration Vector: Social Engineering. Target: Nexus Project Lead. Anomaly: Unusual Pattern in Protocol. Recommendation: Further Investigation Required.*

Before tonight, I assumed my anonymous contact was just a disgruntled Eclipse suit—someone who used "social engineering" to sweet-talk the current Project Lead over drinks, swiping the cryptic message about the Architect's flawed design. 

But looking at the raw data of the Nexus Protocol, that theory falls apart. Eclipse’s internal AI doesn't flag human-to-human watercooler gossip as an *Unusual Pattern in Protocol*. It flags code. It flags network behavior. The "Social Engineering" wasn't a person manipulating the Project Lead in the physical world. It was the *system* manipulating the Project Lead's terminal. 

I stare at the words of the original message burning on my screen: *The architect's design is flawed, but the blueprint remains.*

The Architect is Dr. Aris Thorne. He vanished six months ago. 
The flaw is the biological processing requirement. 
Eclipse solved that flaw by hooking undocumented prisoners into the mainframe as living, breathing processors. 

The pieces snap together with a sickening click. My blood turns to ice. 

Thorne didn't flee Eclipse. He didn't vanish. When he realized what the corporate board intended to do with his predictive model—when he tried to stop them from turning human beings into batteries—they silenced him. But they didn't kill him. They needed his genius. 

Thorne was the first test subject. 

He’s down there. Right now. Wired directly into the dark heart of the Nexus Protocol. 

That explains Block A. The *Unusual Pattern in Protocol* wasn't a glitch; it was Thorne. Using his own hidden backdoor—the blueprint—he managed to scrape together enough localized control within the biological network to reach out. He used the system to "socially engineer" the current Project Lead's secure comms, bypassing the ICE just long enough to push that cryptic message out to my contact. 

The anonymous message wasn't just a tip-off. It was an S.O.S. from a man trapped inside a digital hell of his own making. 

I look up the dark, vertical expanse of the maintenance shaft. Freedom and the rainy rooftop are just fifty feet above me. I have the data. I could expose Eclipse tomorrow and let the authorities handle the fallout. 

But Eclipse owns the authorities. If I leak this, they’ll just purge the sub-levels, incinerate the human servers, and bury Thorne's mind forever before the feds even get a warrant. 

I holster my sidearm and pull a fresh magazine from my vest. The mission parameters just changed. Echo-12 isn't just here for a data heist anymore. 

I'm going back down. I'm going to find the Architect. And I'm going to burn Project Nexus to the ground.
